answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
Give it a full week before you jog, and only if the soreness and blister are gone. The old rule of one easy day per mile raced is overcautious; most coaches aim for roughly a week of walking, a second week of short easy jogs, then build volume gradually.

The Thanksgiving 10K is five weeks out, which is tight but workable if you treat it as a fun race, not a time trial. Week one is walks, week two is short easy jogs, weeks three to four add volume and one short faster session, and week five tapers. If that sounds good, tell me and I will aim the plan there. If you would rather rest longer and pick a bigger goal in the spring, that is fine too.

new.analysis:
## What happened

You executed the taper exactly as planned and raced it bravely, holding 8:32/mi through 20 before the quads went. The back half slowed about 26 s/mi and the last 10K ran around 9:28/mi, which is a classic late-race quad fade, not a fitness problem. Twelve minutes off your first marathon is a real step forward.

## Why 3:45 slipped

You moved the race forward two weeks and only had one 20-miler plus the short 12 the week before. That shortened the final long-run block, and the hilly race (617 ft of climb) taxed the quads earlier than flat courses would. The fitness was close; the specific durability was not quite there yet.

## Why this week looks like it does

Recovery is the training this week. Marathon racing leaves deep muscle damage and immune load, and running on sore legs mostly adds risk without fitness. Walks keep blood moving and mood up without pounding. The short Saturday jog is a test, not a session; if the legs or blister say no, swap it for another walk and we try again next week.

## What I want from you

Tell me whether you want to point at the Thanksgiving 10K or rest longer and pick a bigger target. Either answer is a good one. Also log how you sleep and how the legs feel each day, so next week's plan can lean on real data rather than a guess.

safetyCallouts.title: Normal marathon soreness, but watch it.
safetyCallouts.body: Deep muscle soreness that keeps getting worse after a week, swelling, dark urine, or any sharp pain is not normal recovery; see a doctor or physio if that shows up.

safetyCallouts.title: Care for the blister.
safetyCallouts.body: Keep it clean and covered, and do not jog until it has closed; if it looks red, hot or weepy, see a pharmacist or doctor.
